1#א: Lead. Rashi and Tosafot there 33b and Ketubot 107b and see above siman 135 seif 6 and Orach Chaim siman 491 s.k. 23:
1#ב: Inside. So Tosafot explain there s.v. and the halachah and Shulchan Aruch, and like kunya in chapter 2 (33b) there and chapter kli sheni that it is inside — for if outside the earthenware inside absorbs; and likewise in chapter Avodah Zarah (47b) the rim of kunya, etc.:
1#ג: In a mikveh of, etc. There:
1#ד: Or a spring, etc. Meaning: even though a spring purifies in a kli sheni, as written in Torat Kohanim "these were stated" and "a gathering of water shall be pure" — one might think even if he filled water on his shoulder and made a mikveh, l'chatchila it would be pure; Scripture teaches: a spring — just as a spring is by Heaven's hand, so a mikveh by Heaven's hand; if from a spring a spring purifies in a kli sheni, perhaps a mikveh purifies in a kli sheni? Scripture teaches: however — a spring, a spring purifies in a kli sheni, and a mikveh in forty se'ah; and in the first chapter of Mikvaot mishnah 7 and for a spring, etc.; and there chapter 5 mishnah 1 that the spring, etc.; and mishnah 3 and for a spring, etc.; and likewise Rambam and Raavad; but R. Yitzchak explained: only for vessels that are d'oraisa, even in a mikveh a revi'it suffices, as written in the first chapter of Pesachim (17b), even though they nullified revi'it of a mikveh as written in chapter 6 of Nazir (38a) — the spring remains on Torah law and d'rabbanan is discussed there; and even though they expound a verse in Torat Kohanim, it is a rabbinic support; but a person, even in a spring from the Torah requires forty se'ah, from what is written in chapter 3 of Chagigah (22a), for the ground trembles, etc.; and this applies only to a spring where earth roots connect in water under the ground (and see above siman 201 s.k. 6). And Semak wrote: this is for impurity; but here even in a spring we require forty se'ah, as written "waters in which a niddah immerses," etc.; this is his language there: if it wrote "and it shall be pure," etc. — that is in a spring or revi'it of a mikveh d'oraisa, for "and it shall be pure" is in what was purified from impurity; and this is Tosafot there s.v. waters even in two; and the same applies to a spring, for they are equal d'oraisa:
1#ה: Some say, etc. Semak and as Ran explains: only when coated inside and outside; but otherwise one immerses without a blessing:
2#א: Requires, etc. and if, etc. As written in chapter 8 of Mikvaot: one who holds, etc., and the first tanna; and Rashba explains the first tanna agrees with R. Shimon, only R. Shimon argues with the first tanna that rinsing does not help — unlike Rambam there and in his composition the first tanna argues with R. Shimon and decreed lest he not loosen; for if so, in rings (in Tosefta) chapter 6 of Mikvaot — loose are chatzitzot, not loose are not chatzitzot; and chapter 5 of Shabbat (92b) and they immerse in their place while perforated; and chapter 6 (57a) until he loosens them; and chapter 4 of Yevamot (46a) he loosened them — why do we not decree?
2#ב: And only, etc. See above siman 202 seif 6 in the gloss: be careful, etc.; and likewise, etc.; and Mordechai likewise at the end of Avodah Zarah: when one places glass full of water in a bucket full of water and sinks in a pit, etc.; and as written in chapter 3 of Chagigah (21a) that the vessel's weight is a chatzitzah; he challenged there from what is written in chapter 7 of Mikvaot: he immersed a bed in it, etc.; and he resolved: here the water in the bucket is detached, therefore it does not help; and he wrote: one should also be careful from what is written there, one who holds, etc., as above; and this is why he wrote "and only," etc.; and the rabbi's words require study, for even when moistening in mikveh water they become detached on the hand; and Mordechai's words are thus: there mikveh water preceded under the bed, unlike here where detached preceded and through pouring into the mikveh it purifies, as Rosh wrote there and below siman 198 paragraph 25; and if so they must be loose so mikveh water will reach them, therefore it does not help; and likewise here the place of the vessel he holds must be in mikveh water first and afterward he holds there; but the mishnah's language "and if he rinsed his hand," etc., does not imply thus; and one must say for his words that there he deals with that he is not pressing and holding with force, only he need not loosen — all this is forced, for the mishnah states plainly; and Mordechai's main law requires study — whence do we distinguish between detached and attached; and chapter 3 of Chagigah where there is no water at all in the outer vessel — and the essence is there is no distinction, as the mishnah states here "and if he rinsed" — detached they are, as above; and likewise in the gloss in siman 202 there he did not mention water in the outer vessel; and even with force it helps from what sinks, as above, and as written in siman 198 seif 31:
3#א: He blesses, etc. As written in Tosefta last chapter of Berakhot: one who performs all mitzvos must bless, etc.; and as written in the Gemara in several places: all mitzvos one blesses, etc.; and in the first chapter of Pesachim (7b):
3#ב: And if they, etc. In Tosefta there: an individual who performed ten mitzvos blesses on each one; one who performed a mitzvah all day blesses only once; and in the chapter of covering blood 6b:
4#_: Tripod, etc.; but, etc. As written there: eating vessels are spoken of in the parashah; and Rashba explains: it is written "everything that comes into fire you shall pass through fire," etc. — whatever comes in fire must be made fit through fire; this is an eating vessel that absorbs, etc.; unlike here that does not absorb, like two pots, as written above siman 92 end of seif 8 and end of seif 93; and even though in Orach Chaim siman 491 seif 4 he requires libun — it is a mere stringency because sometimes dough spills on it:
5#א: Knife, etc. From what is written in the first chapter of Chullin (8b): for example, if he heated it in fire — and there is no question; and tevilah, as written in Avodah Zarah there: they heat and immerse, etc.; and as written: eating vessels, etc.; and this is not considered an eating vessel, for it still requires repair by cooking or roasting — "not for a banquet" does not apply. Mordechai there:
5#ב: Or, etc. For it is not specifically of slaughter, for it still requires great repair — flaying; and Rashi there (1a) s.v. and let it be derived, etc.; and the Gemara's language implies thus, for it says "let it be derived" — implying forbidden; and why did the Gemara not ask on permitted slaughter — one may say it holds like those who rinse, and even so forbidden l'chatchila as written there 107b, although the peel, etc.; and Rosh wrote l'chatchila forbidden relying that he will peel; and likewise — but this is a thing possible without rinsing, as written in siman 92 seif 2; therefore it only asked on flaying that is possible by roasting; and Tosafot there 33a s.v. and they are eaten — unlike on Shabbat because of blood on the mouth; and as written in siman 65 seif 5, and great rubbing is required on the mouth that is hard; and why it did not ask on Rava's words — because he did not mention l'chatchila in his words; and this is why Rashi did not explain the prohibition of the slaughterer per Rava — for if so let it ask on permitted, and Rosh's words there already rejected if Rashi meant forbidden and permitted l'chatchila:
5#ג: And some say. For he holds that matter in Chullin when they asked from a non-Jew and need not explain the Gemara there — it must be thus; for if in his sale or pledge it is nullified, as Tur wrote end of seif 139 in the name of R. Yonah and Ramban. And Mordechai holds like Tosafot in chapter 4 of Avodah Zarah 50b s.v. we require; but those brazier vessels, etc. — we establish like the rabbis, etc.; and the same applies, etc.; and Mordechai himself likewise there; but Ran wrote like R. Yitzchak and Ramban that only actual idolatry, as written there 53b, since their value is dear, etc.; unlike implements that are not as dear as actual idolatry; and as written in Tosefta chapter 7: even vessels a woman uses and priests stole and sold them — behold these are permitted; and likewise in the gloss in siman 146 seif 8; and his words here follow his view:
5#ד: The irons, etc. As above, that repair is still required; and he decided here they are not required because it is impossible to use them for another use, unlike a slaughter knife. Shach. And it is incorrect, for a slaughter knife too is not used, as written in Chullin there and Tosafot in chapter 157 of Shabbat 123b s.v. knife. And some say, etc.; and as written in Shulchan Aruch Orach Chaim siman 308. We do not follow here what is fit but the use; and see Chullin; rather it depends on the dispute mentioned and Issur VeHeter's words:
5#ה: But covering, etc. For the broth and steam rise to the cover and it is like a pot; and as written in chapter 25 (108:109) in "he shook and covered"; and likewise for impurity, as written in chapter 5 of Machshirin and chapter 2 there — unlike covering bread; and as written in chapter 2 there: he drank impure water, etc., entered water, etc., dried off, etc.:
6#_: Wooden vessel, etc. Even according to the rabbis in chapter 6 of Shabbat (60a) who say everything follows the stabilizer — here no tevilah is required, since one does not use them via metal, for we require eating vessels; and this is why he wrote "outside," and as written above seif 1 regarding kunya — Tosafot s.v. and the halachah. And like kunya: although its essence is earthenware, we follow the coating; and even though for impurity, metal coating on plain wooden vessels we do not follow the coating and it is pure, as written at the end of Chagigah; and the other answer: the rabbis speak to R. Eliezer, etc.; meaning not only regarding the Temple table that Scripture calls wood and the altar, as Rashi wrote there — rather in all vessels, as written in chapter 11 of Kelim: a lampstand is impure and coated is pure; and there "the rim," etc., and coated are pure; and Rosh strained there that it refers to impure iron — but it is not so, for it does not deal with this, for it says "the rim," etc., of metal are impure — meaning they receive impurity; and likewise the rims before it; and this is what the mishnah in Chagigah means "because they are coated" — meaning R. Eliezer defiles because of the metal in them, and the rabbis purify because the metal is coating; and as written "the rim," etc., and coated are pure; and likewise Rambam there and in his composition chapter 4 of Kelim — only his view is that even for a receiving vessel that receives impurity, the coating nullifies the vessel and it is pure; and the sugya does not imply thus, for it asks on the contrary, etc.; and even for the other answer there is no difficulty, only the coating is nullified to the vessel and as if not coated, and he retracted from what he wrote there "let it be derived from coating," etc. — all this is the first answer; and in the Gemara there, and what he brought proof from Torat Kohanim "every vessel," etc., "I might add coating," etc. — it does not deal with metal, for only wood and leather are written there; and as written in chapter 97 of Kelim: this is the rule — all for coating are pure; and Raavad already challenged; nevertheless his words here are correct that coating is nullified to the vessel; and as written in chapter 11 of the five primary sources of impurity, halachah 11: their coatings are nullified to them; and here we follow the coating because use is in the coating inside:
7#א: Cup of, etc. Since one uses inside the silver — Semak and as above; and even though for kunya he ruled to immerse without a blessing, as written in seif 1 in the gloss — he wrote there because they are only for ornament; and he returned here and in seif 6 from what Beit Yosef ruled and adopted Tosafot's view and Beit HaGadol; and this is what he wrote in the gloss: and likewise a mill, even though in seif 1 he wrote "some say," etc., and so is the practice:
7#ב: And likewise funnels, etc. Meaning: even though they do not receive, as written in chapter 11 of Kelim and chapter 1 of Shabbat and chapter 1 of Chullin (25a) and other places that plain metal vessels are impure:
7#ג: And only, etc. As written in chapter 13 of Kelim: wood serving metal is impure and metal serving wood is pure; and Mordechai in the name of Rambam: their law is like for impurity, as written in the first chapter of Shabbat (15b): glass vessels — why did they decree, etc. — evidently we compare to impurity; and the only difference is eating vessels follow place of use; and Rambam disagrees even in this; but for other tevilat kelim it equals impurity and purity; and this is why he wrote "but a vessel," etc. — we establish like the rabbis who follow the stabilizer; and since the stabilizer is inside — and one may say regarding stabilizer in the first chapter of Shabbat (there) that the sages argue with R. Meir there that one does not stabilize for a vessel except for what is inside, as Tosafot wrote there; and even in this case Mordechai ruled there we follow the stabilizer like R. Meir, as we wrote; and these that are glued, etc.; and although everything follows the stabilizer, this applies where one used via the stabilizer, like a hole that was sealed, etc.; and there Rambam wrote: a pan that was pierced, etc., and his reason: for Rav Ashi in the first chapter of Shabbat (16b) who said: always for earthenware, etc. — the anonymous mishnah of these are chatzitzot comes according to R. Meir; and likewise Rambam in chapter 1 of the five primary sources of Kelim like Rav Ashi, and wrote they have no purification in a mikveh; and this is why he wrote "and without sealing," etc.; but Rav Ashi's law itself requires study, for in Avodah Zarah he holds the reason when they break, etc.; and Tosafot wrote there; and it is difficult to distinguish between tevilah here and tevilah there. And were it not for their words, it would appear we certainly compare them to metal vessels and earthenware vessels; only R. Eliezer does not hold to compare one thing partly to earthenware and partly to metal except for impurity, since its beginning, etc.; but for tevilah, whether new or for purity, earthenware tevilah is not required — compare to metal vessels; and the mishnah mentioned comes according to the rabbis:
8#א: Or a renter. As written: only purchasers; and Rashi there s.v. purchasers and s.v. and as the incident, etc. — unlike renters, for they are not absolute, for "purchasers" is not written to include renters — rental for its day is sale, as written in chapter 4 of Bava Metzia (56b) — rather we learn from the incident that occurred:
8#ב: But, etc. Tosafot s.v. but, etc., that they did not say borrowers except because the non-Jew is still upon it and in his domain:
8#ג: And some, etc. So it appears from Tosafot's words already, etc., for there is no obligation on the second, for it is not purchased in his hand and not his; and this is why he wrote "and likewise," etc.:
9#א: (Lekut) And if not, he immerses it. For we are stringent out of doubt. And Rambam ruled no tevilah is required, per his view that he wrote tevilat kelim is d'rabbanan and the verses are mere support (end of compilation):
9#ב: And if in the end, etc. Also depends on the doubt mentioned; and as written in Challah chapter 4: its stringency is found, etc.:
10#א: And some disagree. For he holds a craftsman acquires through enhancement of the vessel and it is his money; and like Rav Assi in chapter 9 of Bava Kamma (98b); but Rif ruled there like Rava, who concludes there (99b) that all, etc.; and likewise chapter 2 of Kiddushin; and Choshen Mishpat siman 306 seif 2; and Even HaEzer siman 28 seif 15 (and see our rabbi in Choshen Mishpat siman 306 s.k. 8, and from this is proof for Rif's words, etc.; but Rashba in Bava Kamma there rejected this — see there):
10#ב: And one should immerse it, etc. Even according to those who hold it is d'oraisa, the blessing is d'rabbanan and its doubt is lenient; and as written in Orach Chaim siman 436 — see there:
10#ג: And if part, etc. And so from Tosafot's words mentioned above, for he thought because a craftsman acquires through enhancement of the vessel he is liable:
10#ד: And likewise a craftsman, etc. Also depends on the dispute mentioned; but requires study, for even if he acquires he acquires only the enhancement; and Rashi in Bava Metzia 112a s.v. craftsman, etc.; and he wrote above "and if part," etc.; and as Issur VeHeter wrote: whatever has part of the non-Jew in it has the law of the non-Jew's; and as written in seif 11 in the gloss: Jew and non-Jew, etc.; and if he bought it afterward he is liable; and likewise it is difficult from what he wrote "or he gave part," etc.; and Peri Chadash likewise challenged:
11#ב: But, etc. There we establish in chapter 2 of Pesachim (31b): a Jew from a non-Jew and a non-Jew from a Jew do not acquire a pledge; only a pledge from a non-Jew — even borrowers are thought liable, for "purchasers" is not written in Scripture except like the incident that occurred when they were decided for them; and the same applies to a pledge; but the non-Jew's must be absolute:
11#ג: Jew, etc. For he does not emerge from impurity through this tevilah, for the non-Jew is still upon it; and as written in the Yerushalmi that tevilah is that he emerge from the impurity of the non-Jew to the sanctity of Israel; and Ran:
11#ד: A Jew whom they stole, etc.; but, etc. For the owners' name already sank from him — unlike a thief or robber; and as written in chapter 7 of Kilayim: from when is it called, etc.; and in the Yerushalmi there R. Acha said: they sank and did not despair — its prohibition; R. Tarfon: they despaired and did not sink — its prohibition — d'rabbanan, meaning because of mar'it ha'ayin and not by law; and see above siman 296 seif 6:
12#_: Requires, etc. Chapter 10 of Mikvaot mishnah 5: all handles, etc.:
13#א: Must remove, etc. Mordechai there; and Rosh chapter 25 in the name of Sifri — it is not in our Sifri; and in Yalkut it exists: only the gold He said — only to remove their rust:
13#ב: If he is particular, etc. and if, etc. As written at the beginning of Eruvin (4b) and Sukkah and Yevamot and Niddah:
14#א: We do not believe, etc. For tevilat kelim is d'oraisa, as written in the Gemara there, and so most poskim; and a minor regarding what is not in his hand is not believed even for d'rabbanan, as written in chapter 2 of Ketubot; and these are believed, etc., but not young minors; and likewise chapter 5 of Eruvin (58b): even a slave, etc., but not a minor; but regarding what is in his hand he is believed for d'rabbanan, as written in the first chapter of Pesachim (4b): they trusted him, etc.; and it implies specifically for d'rabbanan, although slave and maidservant are believed even for d'oraisa; and there it does not say specifically d'rabbanan, only because there is trouble, as Yerushalmi writes — this refers only to men and slaves; and Yerushalmi there: some do not teach women because they are lazy and they check — all the more so minors, because they are not believed for d'oraisa; and so Tosafot there; and Tosafot in Eruvin 31b s.v. here. Therefore it appears to explain, etc. (and see end of siman 127):
14#ב: But, etc. As written there: standing and seeing him, and intent for tevilah is not required; even if they fell by themselves into water it suffices; and as written in chapter 2 of Chullin (31); and Rav — Rav Nachman holds like him there and in chapter 2 of Chagigah; and as the poskim wrote; and even if it fell from a bridge, as we wrote for R. Natan that we establish like him; and intent is not required:
15#א: If he immersed, etc. As above in the preceding seif; and in Even HaEzer; and as Beit HaGadol wrote, unlike Shach (and Maharshal is not necessary, as the later authorities wrote):
15#ב: But he is not, etc. As written above siman 118: he is not believed neither to be lenient nor stringent:
16#_: And if he transgressed, etc. Tosafot there s.v. and all of them, etc.; and even for the view they wrote "however," etc. — that is for those who hold ntiluf is forbidden; and so in the Gemara there it says: one taught, etc., and it answers nothing on tevilah; and one must say either the first view that it teaches and only asks about hag'alah and libun, or the latter view; and even though in Rosh there at the beginning of his words it appears the latter baraita refers only to hag'alah and libun — the Gemara's plain meaning does not imply thus, and he only wrote for clarity:
